taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 231, Conium maculatum: stems upright, much branched, 5 dm to 30 dm tall.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 231, Conium maculatum: umbels 2.5 cm to 7.5 cm across on slender rays 2.5 cm to 4 cm long; the genus has many-rayed compound umbels (p. 230).

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: leaves 20 cm to 50 cm long.

traits.leaf_division.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 231, Conium maculatum: all the leaves pinnately cut, the divisions ovate in outline and thin.

traits.division_pattern.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 231, Conium maculatum: all the leaves pinnately cut, the divisions ovate in outline and thin.

traits.division_order.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 216, Conium, in the key to genera: leaves cut again and again into small segments; drawn three times divided (three to four in the photos).

traits.pinnae.note: Eleven primary divisions, five pairs and a terminal one (4 to 6 pairs in the photos), set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 107741349, 202447808, 243333317, 25579621, 304969302, 312417, 40221962, 75390188): the floras give no count or measure.

traits.pinnules.note: Seven pinnules to each primary division, each pinna deltoid-lanceolate, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 107741349, 202447808, 243333317, 25579621, 304969302, 312417, 40221962, 75390188): the floras give no count or measure.

traits.leaflets.note: Seven lobes to each pinnule, which is deeply pinnately cut, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 107741349, 202447808, 243333317, 25579621, 304969302, 312417, 40221962, 75390188): the floras give no count or measure.

traits.terminal_leaflet.note: Each division ending in one elongated segment, set by hand from the photos: Abrams (1951 p. 231) does not say.

traits.division_planes.note: Flat, fern-like sprays, each pinna close to one plane, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 107741349, 202447808, 243333317, 25579621, 304969302, 312417, 40221962, 75390188): the floras give no count or measure.

traits.leaf_shape.note: The whole leaf broadly triangular, about 1.1-1.3 times as long as wide (Abrams p. 231: the divisions ovate in outline), set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 107741349, 202447808, 243333317, 25579621, 304969302, 312417, 40221962, 75390188): the floras give no count or measure.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 231, Conium maculatum: the last divisions toothed or cut.

traits.leaflet_length_m.note: Lobes 3 mm to 8 mm long, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 107741349, 202447808, 243333317, 25579621, 304969302, 312417, 40221962, 75390188): the floras give no count or measure.

traits.leaflet_width_m.note: Lobes 1.5 mm to 3 mm wide, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 107741349, 202447808, 243333317, 25579621, 304969302, 312417, 40221962, 75390188): the floras give no count or measure.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 230, Conium: tall, hairless, poisonous biennials with spotted stems.

traits.flower_colour.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 230, Conium: small white flowers; sRGB by eye.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 231, Conium maculatum: fruit 2 mm to 2.5 mm long.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 231, Conium maculatum: in waste places, mostly damp ground, through the Pacific States, flowering May to July.

traits.life_span.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 230, Conium: tall biennials.

appearance.organs.flower.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 231, Conium maculatum: umbels 2.5 cm to 7.5 cm across, slender rays 2.5 cm to 4 cm long, small white flowers. Drawn as umbellets of 15 small white flowers.

generator.params.note: Cow parsnip's values, changed by hand for poison hemlock: a tall stem over a few large basal leaves, its leaves on petioles sheathing at the base (Abrams 1951 p. 231), ending in a white compound umbel. Abrams's stems are much branched, each branch ending in an umbel; the herb program grows no side branches, so the stem is drawn unbranched with its one umbel. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 1.5 m tall in its second (flowering) year in the open, within Abrams's 5-30 dm. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye, after Abrams (1951 pp. 230-231): hairless, dark green, finely divided leaves; green stems (their purple spots are not drawn); white flowers. The leaves broadly triangular, the lowest pinnae longest and the topmost a fifth as long (largest 0, lowest 0.2), from iNaturalist photos (observations 107741349, 202447808, 243333317, 25579621, 304969302, 312417, 40221962, 75390188).
